detailed_rationale:
Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL) was demerged from Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail (ABFRL) effective 1-May-2025, inheriting ABFRL's legacy 'cash cow' formal/lifestyle apparel brands - Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England and Simon Carter - plus emerging growth bets in Van Heusen innerwear, the Reebok sportswear licence and American Eagle youth-western-wear. As of March 2026 the business runs a large physical footprint (3,348 brand stores, 4.9mn sq ft, 39,500+ multi-brand outlets, 6,500+ shop-in-shops). FY26 - its first full year as a standalone listed entity - saw consolidated revenue of Rs 8,395.8cr, up 7% YoY (Q4 alone: Rs 2,174cr, +12% YoY), with EBITDA growing faster than revenue (+13-14% YoY to Rs 1,429cr for the year, Rs 375cr in Q4) - genuine, if modest, operating leverage on mature legacy brands. Reported PAT surged 185% YoY to Rs 171cr, but one tracker explicitly notes that PAT/PBT normalised for FY26 excludes a one-time exceptional item tied to the 'Statutory Impact of New Labour Code' - i.e., part of the headline PAT jump is a disclosed one-off rather than pure operating improvement, and the true underlying profit growth is more modest than the 185% headline suggests (magnitude/direction of the item not independently confirmed beyond the exceptional-item flag itself, so we have not built it into the growth number below).

The balance sheet shows D/E of 2.14x, which for a store-network apparel/retail business is influenced by Ind-AS 116 lease-liability capitalisation (a general accounting feature of large physical-retail-footprint businesses, not necessarily company-specific distress) alongside working-capital needs typical of a multi-brand apparel portfolio; interest coverage of 3.69x is adequate but not generous. ROCE is strong (29.7%) and the quality score (67.4) is the most respectable in this batch, reflecting the mature, reasonably profitable core brand portfolio. The valuation (PE ~67.7x, value_score 34.9/100) prices in continued margin expansion and some contribution from the newer brands (Reebok, American Eagle, innerwear), on top of only mid-single-digit-to-low-double-digit legacy-brand revenue growth.
recommendation_rationale: This is a genuinely higher-quality business than most in this batch (strong ROCE, respectable quality score) built on durable legacy brands, but revenue growth is modest (7% FY26) and part of the standout PAT growth figure is flagged as a one-off exceptional item rather than pure operating improvement. At ~68x trailing earnings, the valuation already requires sustained margin expansion and real contribution from the newer brand bets to be justified, and we do not see enough margin of safety in the numbers to override the quant Sell.
summary: ABLBL owns some of India's most established formal-wear brands and delivered steady, if unspectacular, revenue growth with genuine margin improvement in its first year as a standalone company, though part of its reported profit jump reflects a one-off accounting item rather than pure operating gains. At its current valuation, we recommend Sell.
positive_para: ABLBL sits on a portfolio of decades-old, trusted brands (Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England) with a large, established retail footprint, strong ROCE (29.7%), and genuine EBITDA margin expansion (EBITDA growing faster than revenue in both Q4 and FY26). The Reebok and American Eagle brand licences and the innerwear business offer incremental growth optionality beyond the mature core.
negative_para: Revenue growth is modest for the valuation on offer (7% FY26, low-double-digit in Q4), and part of the headline 185% PAT jump is flagged by at least one tracker as including a one-off exceptional item related to the new Labour Code's statutory impact - meaning normalised profit growth is meaningfully lower than the reported figure suggests. Legacy formal-wear brands also face a structurally maturing category as casual/athleisure wear gains share, and D/E of 2.14x plus only 3.69x interest coverage leave a modest, not generous, cushion.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At ~68x trailing earnings, the multiple requires several years of continued margin expansion plus a real growth contribution from the newer brand bets (Reebok, American Eagle, innerwear) layered on top of mature, mid-single-digit legacy-brand growth. The business quality supports a premium to the sector, but not obviously this large a one relative to the modest top-line trajectory shown so far. Judgment: rich-to-fair - a good business priced for more growth than it has yet demonstrated.
